               <ns0:p n="34">34 Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seing I know not a Man?<ns0:note place="bottom">There are some would excuse <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> in this reply and tell us these Words spake in her no doubt, that the things spoken by the Angel should not come to pass, only <ns0:hi>admiration,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>desire</ns0:hi> to be further, which way God would effect such a wonder of <ns0:hi>Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence.</ns0:hi> Others think her Words hardly excuseable from all guilt, tho the more excuseable, because there had yet been no such Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sident made in the World of the Divine Power, as to cause a <ns0:hi>Virgin to conceive, and bring forth a Son.</ns0:hi> The next Words<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Seeing I know not a Man,</ns0:hi> seem to import, that she understood the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> of the present or past time, that she had already con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived, or should immediately conceive, against which she objects her not having any carnal knowledge of any Man. For the Notion of some <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> that would from hence impose upon us to believe, from hence, that <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> had <ns0:hi>vowed Virginity,</ns0:hi> as if the sense of th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Words were. <ns0:hi>I am resolved never to know Man,</ns0:hi> it is so ridiculous<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that no Man of ordinary sense can allow it, for, besides that there wa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> no such <ns0:hi>vows,</ns0:hi> that we ever read of amongst the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> nor could any such be made but by the Law of God, might be res<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cinded, if made when the Virgin was in her Fathers house: and besides that, it is very improbable, that a Jewish Woman should make such a Vow, in whom barrenness was such a reproach, and who lookt upon it as a curse; I say besides these things, who can have such unworthy thoughts of the blessed Virgin, as to think that she should, having made such a vow, admit of an espousal to <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> to mock him. But she certainly understood the Angel, as speaking of a thing <ns0:hi>in being,</ns0:hi> or which presently should be, and tho she believed what the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> said, yet is desirous of further satisfaction how such a thing could be, out of the ordinary course of Nature.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And the angel answered and said unto her, The holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that Holy thing which shall be born of thee, shall be called theSon of God.<ns0:note place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> (who is also called here <ns0:hi>the Power of the Highest,</ns0:hi>) shall <ns0:hi>come upon thee</ns0:hi>; it is a Phrase which signifieth a <ns0:hi>special and peculiar influence of the holy Spirit</ns0:hi>; thus we read of the Prophets, <ns0:hi>That the Spirit of the Lord came upon them,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 20.14, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> which argued a special Influence of the Holy Spirit on them, efficacious, so as it put them upon a present Prophe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cying. There is a common influence of God upon the forming of all Children in the Womb, <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 10.8. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 139.5. But this Phrase denoteth, an extraordinary special influence of the Spirit, changing the order and course of Nature, and giving a Power to the Blood of the Virgin by him sanctified, to coagulate alone to the forming of a body of a Child; this is more Mysteriously yet exprest, by the next term <ns0:hi>over shadow thee,</ns0:hi> which I take to be a modest Phrase, signifying only a supply of Mans act, by a Divine creating Power<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> in a most miraculous manner. <ns0:hi>There<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore also that holy thing, which shall be born of thee, shall be called the Son of God,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> was called the Son of God, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3. God (by his creating Power) supplying as to him the place of <ns0:hi>Fathe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> and Mother,</ns0:hi> and to <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> supplying the place of the <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> tho not of the Mother, for (saith the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi>) he shall be <ns0:hi>born of thee.</ns0:hi> But yet that <ns0:hi>Mass of Flesh,</ns0:hi> shall be an <ns0:hi>holy thing,</ns0:hi> because tho born of thee, and Flesh of thy Flesh, yet of thy Flesh first sanctified, by the Holy Ghost coming upon and over-shadowing of thee. He shall be <ns0:hi>called so,</ns0:hi> not that he was not so by eternal Generation, (of which the Angel here speaks not,) but the <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi> the eternal Son of God, which was in the be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gining, being thus made Flesh, and personally united to thy Flesh, the whole Person shall be called, <ns0:hi>The Son of God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And behold, thy cousin Elizabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth moneth with her who was called barren.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 18.14. Jer. 32.17. Chap. 18.27.</ns0:note> with God nothing shall be unpossible.<ns0:note place="bottom">What a particular notice doth God take of the Children of Men? he knoweth our Relations. <ns0:hi>Thy Cousin Elizabeth.</ns0:hi> Here some make a question how <ns0:hi>Elizabeth,</ns0:hi> who <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1. was one of the Daughters of <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> and consequently of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> could be <ns0:hi>Cousin</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> who was of the house of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and conse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quently of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iuda,</ns0:hi> (as our Evangelist proveth <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.) because of the Law <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 36.6.7. But <ns0:hi>Cousin</ns0:hi> may be taken in a large sense as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> calleth all the Jews <ns0:hi>his kinsmen, Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.10. or they might be Cousins in astrict sense, for the Daughters of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> might marry into any other Tribes, having no <ns0:hi>inheritance</ns0:hi> to carry away, to prevent which was the Law, <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 36. <ns0:hi>And this is the sixth Month,</ns0:hi> &c. from her conception, by which time Women use to be at some certainty about their Quickening, you must not therefore think this <ns0:hi>impossible,</ns0:hi> for you know <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> was counted barren, and was old, yet she hath conceived. <ns0:hi>And with God nothing is impossible.</ns0:hi> I bring you a message from God, to whom all things are possible. This was an ordinary saying, amongst them, <ns0:hi>Nothing is impossible with God.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour useth it several times <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 10.27. <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 19.26. Nor needed we any Scripture to prove that nothing could be impossible to him who is the first Being, the first Cause, and the Fountain of all Power, and to whom all things are subject. No considerate Man will from hence conclude that things are <ns0:hi>possible</ns0:hi> to God, which would derogate from the perfection of the Divine being, and are imperfections in us. Nor yet that any thing is possible to God, the co<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>trary to which he hath willed but God can do whatsoever he can will.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:294" />38 And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord, be unto me according to thy word. And the angel de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>arted from her.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Once ha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e I spoken</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Iob. Ch.</ns0:hi> 40.5.) <ns0:hi>but I will not An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer.</ns0:hi> In like manner the Virgin speaketh. I will dispute no more<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> I am the Lords Servant, let him do with me, whatsoever he pleaseth. This Phrase, <ns0:hi>Behold the handmaid of the Lord,</ns0:hi> doth not speak her, <ns0:hi>the Lady and Queen of Heaven,</ns0:hi> (as the <ns0:hi>Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />p<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>sts</ns0:hi> stile her) but it speaketh her <ns0:hi>Humility</ns0:hi> and readiness to give up her self to the Lords pleasure, her <ns0:hi>assent,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>consent</ns0:hi> unto God, She addeth a <ns0:hi>Prayer,</ns0:hi> that God would do according to what the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> had said unto her. The Angel having dispatched his errand, and obtained what he came for, ascendeth into Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And Mary arose in those days, and went into the hill-country with hast, into a city of Juda.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And entred into the house of Zacharias, and sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />luted Elizabeth.<ns0:note place="bottom">Many think that this City where this <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> lived was <ns0:hi>He<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bron,</ns0:hi> before called <ns0:hi>Kiriat<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>-Arba, Iosh.</ns0:hi> 14.15. for that was a City, in the Mountanous part of <ns0:hi>Iuda,</ns0:hi> one of the <ns0:hi>Cities of refuge,</ns0:hi> and belonging to the Priests <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 20.7. But whether it was so or no cannot be certainly determined, she probably went not only to rejoyce with <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> her kinswoman, but also to strengthen her own Faith, as to the Revelation which she had received finding that true, which the Angel had told her, con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning her Cousin <ns0:hi>E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>izabeth.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And it came to pass that when Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb: and Elizabeth was filled with the holy Ghost.<ns0:note place="bottom">The motion of the Child in the Womb of the Mother, after her time of quickening is past, and the more then ordinary motion of it, upon some extraordinary cause of joy, is no unusual thing with Women in those circumstances, but doubtless as this<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> motion was more then ordinary, so it had a more then ordinary cause, being caused from the Holy Spirit of God, and so the best Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preters Judge, what is afterward said of <ns0:hi>Elizabeth,</ns0:hi> that she was filled with the <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> is expounded in the next Words, where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in she Prophecieth, of the Spirit of Prophecy.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> thou among women, and blessed <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the fruit of thy womb.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> useth the same Words to <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> which the Angel had used for her, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28. That is thou art an exceeding happy Woman, not only renowned, but one whom God hath greatly favoured and exceeding Blessed and made happy, and <ns0:hi>Blessed is the fruit of thy Womb.</ns0:hi> Tho the same Word be used, yet is not to be understood of the same degree of Ble<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sing. Christ was anointed with the oil of gladness, above his fellows, and Blessed in another sense, and after another manner, then any creature can be said to be Blessed, for the fulness of the Godhead dwelt in him bodily.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 And whence <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> in these Words acknowledgeth both the incarnation of Christ, and the Union of the <ns0:hi>Divine,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Humane Nature,</ns0:hi> in the one Person of the <ns0:hi>Mediator,</ns0:hi> she acknowledgeth <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> her <ns0:hi>Lord,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> to be his Mother.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 For lo, assoon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy.<ns0:note place="bottom">By these Words <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> declareth, that she looked upon the motion of the Child in her Womb, upon <ns0:hi>Marys</ns0:hi> salutation of her, as something more then Natural.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 A<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>d blessed <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> she that believed, <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>here shall be a perfor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mance.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some will have this given as a reason, why <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nounced her <ns0:hi>B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>essed.</ns0:hi> Because she believed, that what God had said should have its effect, as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.28. when the Women Blessed the Womb that bare Christ, and the <ns0:hi>Papps that gave him Suck</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Christ saith, <ns0:hi>yea rather B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>essed are they<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that near the Word of God and keep it. Mary</ns0:hi> was Blessed not in this so much, that she brought forth Christ, as in this that she <ns0:hi>believed in him.</ns0:hi> The Words are certainly a great con<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rmation of what the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> had before told her, and it must needs be a great satisfaction to her, to hear her kinswoman by the Spirit of Prophecy, coming extraordinarily upon her, confirming what the Angel had before told her.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 And Mary said, My soul doth magnifie the Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 And my spirit hath rejoyced in God my Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour.<ns0:note place="bottom">We are now come to the Famous Song of the blessed Virgin, upon whom also the <ns0:hi>Spirit</ns0:hi> of the Lord comes upon this occasion. Shee first Solemnly gives praise unto God, then by various ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressions declareth the Power, and goodness of God, shewing him worthy to be praised and lastly applieth what she had spoke more generally, to the particular business of Mans Redemption. Our <ns0:hi>magnifying God,</ns0:hi> is not by making him great, as he magnifieth us, as it is <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 49. but by declaring, and shewing forth his great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness. She saith, <ns0:hi>her Soul did Magnify the Lord,</ns0:hi> and her <ns0:hi>Spirit rejoyced.</ns0:hi> Soul and Spirit are but two Words, signifying the same thing, and importing that she glorified God <ns0:hi>heartily,</ns0:hi> and with her whole Soul, and teaching us that all praising of God, with our lips, are of no significancy, whithout the conjunction of the heart, with the tongue. [<ns0:hi>In God my Saviour.</ns0:hi>] So <ns0:hi>Hannah</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2.1. <ns0:hi>My heart rejoyceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord.</ns0:hi> This is true, spiritual rejoycing, when the primary object of our joy is not the <ns0:hi>sensible Good,</ns0:hi> but the Goodness of the Lord to us, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> giving us that good thing.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 For he hath regarded the low estate of his hand<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />maiden: for behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our translators have here rightly translated <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. <ns0:hi>Low estate. Mary</ns0:hi> doubtless doth not here commend her own <ns0:hi>Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mility,</ns0:hi> (as some <ns0:hi>Pap<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>sts</ns0:hi> would have it,) but magnifieth God, for that he had respect to her, who was of so mean and low a condition, for tho she was of the family of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> yet that Family had for many years been broken and afflicted, and she was now espoused to a <ns0:hi>Carpenter,</ns0:hi> which spake her condition low and mean, tho de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scended from the <ns0:hi>Royal Family of David,</ns0:hi> and thus God usually magnifieth himself, he chuseth <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> from the Sheepfold to be King over Israel, he much delighteth to exalt such as are low, <ns0:hi>he chooseth the foolish things of the World, to confound the Wise, the weak things of the World to confound the mighty, and base things of the World, and things which are despised, hath God chosen</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1, 28. <ns0:hi>That no flesh should Glory in his presence, v.</ns0:hi> 29. <ns0:hi>Henceforth</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Mary) all generations shall call me Blessed.</ns0:hi> It is no mean favour of God, when God giveth us a name in the World, and that not only in the present <ns0:hi>generation but in succeding Generations.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 For he that is mighty hath done to me great things and holy <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> his name.<ns0:note place="bottom">That which is observable both in this Verse, and in this whole Song, is how the blessed Virgin, attributes all to God, and ascrib<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth nothing to her self, or any merits of her own, much like unto her Father <ns0:hi>David Psal.</ns0:hi> 115.1. <ns0:hi>Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy name give Glory, for thy Mercy, and truths sake,</ns0:hi> and herein she teacheth those Generations, which she had even now said should call her <ns0:hi>Blessed,</ns0:hi> how to take notice of her, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> as one highly favoured of the Lord, one for whom God indeed had done great things, but not as one who had merited any thing at Gods hand, much less as one to whom we should pay a greater Devotion, then to her Son, and speak to her that she should <ns0:hi>command her Son,</ns0:hi> (according to the blasphemous devotion, and Idolatry of the <ns0:hi>Papists, Mary</ns0:hi> is very careful of giving succeeding Generations any occosion from her expressions for any such Superstitions. <ns0:hi>And holy is his Name.</ns0:hi> Holy, that is <ns0:hi>glorious,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>venerable,</ns0:hi> [his name] that is, he himself is Glorious, and Holy, far above the Conception and Comprehension of poor Creatures.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 20.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> his mercy <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> on them that fear him, from generation to generation.<ns0:note place="bottom">Having celebrated God for his <ns0:hi>Glory</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Majesty,</ns0:hi> she here cele<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />brateth him for his <ns0:hi>Mercy,</ns0:hi> which extends to all but especially is shewed to such as fear him, she certainly respecteth the promise of God, to be the God of <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>his seed,</ns0:hi> but declareth this to be most eminently made good to those who are truly Pious, all Piety being expressed ordinarily in Scripture, (especially in the old Testament) under the notion of the <ns0:hi>fear of God,</ns0:hi> we have almost the same Words <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 103.17. It is elsewhere expressed under the notion of <ns0:hi>thousands Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.6. signifying not only the ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tent of the Divine goodness to all his People, but the continu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ance of it for ever.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 51.9 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 52.10.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 33.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 1 Pet. 5.5.</ns0:note> He hath shewed strength with his arm, he hath scattered the proud, in the imagination of their hearts.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 2.6. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Job. 5.11. Psal. 113.6.</ns0:note> He hath put down the mighty from <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> seats, and exalted them of low degree.<ns0:note place="bottom">In these verses the Virgin celebrateth both the Power and justice of God, as she before had done his <ns0:hi>Holiness</ns0:hi> and his Mercy, and Godness. The strength of a Man is much seen in the <ns0:hi>effects</ns0:hi> of his <ns0:hi>arm</ns0:hi>; hence God, who hath no such part as we have, is yet spoken of as if he had an <ns0:hi>arm,</ns0:hi> by which no more is signified, then a <ns0:hi>mighty Power,</ns0:hi> by which he bringeth things to pass. <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 15.16. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40.10 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 89.13. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 98.1. So in many other texts. <ns0:hi>He hath scattered the proud in the imaginations of their hearts: Iethro</ns0:hi> Exod. 18.11. <ns0:hi>knew that the Lord was above all Gods, because in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Proud</ns0:hi> in Scripture often signifies wicked men, as <ns0:hi>the humble</ns0:hi> signifies good and holy men, but <ns0:hi>Proud</ns0:hi> in a strict sense, signifieth Men that have an high opinion of themselves, now there is nothing that a <ns0:hi>Proud Man</ns0:hi> dealeth more Proudly in, then in following the imaginations of his own heart. There (saith <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi>) God <ns0:hi>scattereth them,</ns0:hi> turning their Counsels into folly, and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ounding them in their own imaginations. <ns0:hi>He hath put down the mighty from their Seat,</ns0:hi> thus he did by <ns0:hi>Pharoah, Nebuchad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nezar,</ns0:hi> &c. he pulls down some, and sets up others. Promotion is not from the East, nor from the West, <ns0:hi>and exalteth them of low degree,</ns0:hi> this is Gods way, thus he exalted <ns0:hi>Moses, Ioseph, Iacob, David.</ns0:hi> God thus sheweth his mighty Power, and su<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perintendency upon mens affairs. He doth what he pleaseth with Men, yet what he doth is infinitely <ns0:hi>Wise just</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>good.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:294" />53 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 34.10. 1 Sam 2.5.</ns0:note> He hath filled the hungry with good things, and the rich he hath sent empty away.<ns0:note place="bottom">In this Sentence, the holy Virgin celebrateth, the equity of God in the Government of the World, proportioning Men in some degrees one to another, that the rapacious qualities of some, might not gain all to them, while others have nothing. The Notion of <ns0:hi>hungry,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Persons in want, and <ns0:hi>craving a supp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y.</ns0:hi> The Notion of <ns0:hi>Rich,</ns0:hi> signifieth Persons that are <ns0:hi>full.</ns0:hi> God blesseth the Poor, pitieth the needy, while he neglecteth greater Persons. Some apply it to those whom <ns0:hi>Christ blesseth, Matth.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>who hunger and thirst after Righteousness,</ns0:hi> and ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pound the rich of those who think they have no need of the <ns0:hi>Righteousness of Christ.</ns0:hi> In this sense it is also true, but whither the Virgin intended it here or no I know not.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="54">54 He hath holpen his servant Israel, in <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 31.3.20.</ns0:note> remem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />brance of <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> mercy.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="55">55 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 132.11.</ns0:note> As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever.<ns0:note place="bottom">In these verses the blessed Virgin celebrateth Gods <ns0:hi>mercy</ns0:hi> toge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther with his <ns0:hi>truth,</ns0:hi> withal she hath here a respect to Gods parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular goodness, and Mercy in the sending of the Redeemer. The Word which we here translate <ns0:hi>hath helped,</ns0:hi> signifieth <ns0:hi>he hath sustained,</ns0:hi> or as it were <ns0:hi>lifted up with his hand,</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Servant Israel,</ns0:hi> or his child <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> he calleth <ns0:hi>Ephraim, his dear Son,</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>pleasant Child.</ns0:hi> But by <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> he meaneth <ns0:hi>Believers,</ns0:hi> those of <ns0:hi>Abrahams seed</ns0:hi> that lived in the Faith hope, and expectation of the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> the children of the Promise, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.8. those who are <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> inwardly <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.29. the <ns0:hi>true Circumcision. Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.3. <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> indeed <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.47. This she saith God had done, not in remembrance of their merits, but his own <ns0:hi>Mercy Ezek.</ns0:hi> 36.32. but of his own <ns0:hi>free goodness,</ns0:hi> and Mercy, and in the <ns0:hi>fulfilling of his Promise,</ns0:hi> made to <ns0:hi>Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.15. the extent of which Promise is declared <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.6, 7, 8, 9. and that <ns0:hi>seed of Abraham,</ns0:hi> his seed as the <ns0:hi>Father of the Faithfull</ns0:hi> shall be for ever, and the vertue of the Promise shall hold to them for ever.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="56">56 And Mary abode with her about three moneths, and returned to her own house.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is most probable that she staid with her until she was brought to Bed, not leaving her just at the time of her travail, but she staid not long after but went home, by this time she must her self know that she was with Child, and here in the true order of the History cometh in what we had <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24. See the Notes there.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="57">57 Now Elizabeths full time came, that she should be delivered, and she brought forth a son.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="58">58 And her neighbours, and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>er.</ns0:hi> 14.</ns0:note> they rejoyced with her.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Angel told <ns0:hi>Mary v.</ns0:hi> 36. <ns0:hi>That it was then the sixth Moneth with her,</ns0:hi> after this <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> was with her about three Moneths, which made up her full time, so she was delivered, and brought forth a Son to shew the truth of Gods promises, that we may all learn to give credit to his Word. For the Neighbours and kinswomen of <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> to come, and to rejoyce with her, was but according to the ordinary custom of friends to this Day, like enough to hold to the end of the World. But the Religion of Persons in that age possibly is not in so ordinary a practice, in I mean the taking notice, of the influence and goodness of God to those who receive such Mercies, we are fallen into an age, where con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gratulations are made to Friends, upon any good things happening to them are ordinary, and meetings also to <ns0:hi>make merry,</ns0:hi> (as they call it) upon such occasions, but ah! how little is that God, who openeth the Womb, and a reward from whom Children are, taken notice of? how little is his Power, and goodness in such Providences taken notice of, in such meetings? and made the sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ject of the discourses there had? <ns0:hi>Elizabeths</ns0:hi> Neighbours and Cousins, take notice <ns0:hi>how the Lord had shewed great Mercy unt<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> her.</ns0:hi> The Mercy of a Child, of a safe delivery in the Birth of a Child, are great Mercies, and ought to be the first and principal things taken notice of, in such rejoycing meetings, otherwise the Meeting is more like a Meeting of <ns0:hi>Pagans,</ns0:hi> then of Christi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="59">59 And it came to pass, that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child; and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="60">60 And his mother answered and said, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 13.</ns0:note> Not <ns0:hi>so</ns0:hi>; but he shall be called John.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="61">61 And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Law for Circumcision <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.12. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 12.3. was strictly for it to be performed the <ns0:hi>eigth day.</ns0:hi> We find nothing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> commanded in Scripture, either as to the Person who was to per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />form the office of the Circumciser, or as to the place, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 4.24.25. God met <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Inn,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>sought to kill him,</ns0:hi> because he had not Circumcised his Child, and <ns0:hi>Zipporah his Wife</ns0:hi> did it. It is said they afterwards did it in the <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> but there is no Divine Law in the case. That the name was given to the Child upon its Circumcision, appeareth not from Scripture. It is said <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 21.3.4. that <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> called his Son <ns0:hi>Isaac,</ns0:hi> and then <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>he Circumcised his Son</ns0:hi> Isaac <ns0:hi>being eight Days old,</ns0:hi> we read of no name given by <ns0:hi>Zipporath,</ns0:hi> to her Child when she Circumcised him. But the name was at <ns0:hi>Circumcision</ns0:hi> declared. It is most certain that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was circumcised in his Fathers house, for we find his <ns0:hi>Mother</ns0:hi> was present, who at that time, was not in a condition to stir abroad. They called his name <ns0:hi>Zacharias,</ns0:hi> whence we may observe the ancient usage of giving to children, the names of their Fathers, and kindred. This in all probability is the reason of so many odd, and unjustifiable Names given to Persons, (such as are Names of Heathenish Gods and Goddesses, not fit to be named amongst Christians, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>) We derive from <ns0:hi>Pagans,</ns0:hi> and tho some Heathens changed their Names, when they turned Christians, yet many (probably) did not, and by a long tra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duction, (the Names of Parents being given to Children) the Names of Pagan Idols, such as <ns0:hi>Fortune, Diana,</ns0:hi> and the like, are by a most <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ordid practice made the Names of Christians, a thing which certainly ought to be reformed, for it is a doing honour to those Idols, if the giving a Persons Name to a Child, be (as we ordinarily account it, (an honour done to the Person whose Name is so given. The Jews from their beginning seem to have had a R<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ligion as to this, giving Names to their Children, either significative of Gods mercy to them, or their Children, or their own duty to God, and the Names of the Parents, or some of the kindred, were in honour to them given to their Children, there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore when <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> (who knew the Counsel of God as to this Child, either by some Writing from <ns0:hi>Zachariah,</ns0:hi> or some <ns0:hi>Reve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation</ns0:hi> to her self) heard them call him <ns0:hi>Zachariah,</ns0:hi> she contra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dicted them in this thing, and nameth him <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> they object that none of her kindred was called by that name.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="62">62 And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="63">63 And he asked for a writing-table, and wrote, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Ver.</ns0:hi> 13.</ns0:note> His name is John. And they marvelled all.<ns0:note place="bottom">It was the Parents place, the Fathers especially) to give Child<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren their Names, <ns0:hi>Zachariah</ns0:hi> was Dumb as yet, they therefore make Signs to him, he by Writing declareth, that his Name was <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> that is, He was so named already by the <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> therefore there was to be no further dispute about it. The Friends marvel at the consent of both the Parents in the case, declining all the Names of their kindred.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="64">64 And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue <ns0:hi>loosed,</ns0:hi> and he spake, and praised God.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Angel <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. inflicted the Punishment upon him no longer, then until what he had said should be performed, now it was performed, God looseth his tongue, and <ns0:hi>he praiseth God,</ns0:hi> by the Song which we shall by and by meet with.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="65">65 And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>things.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judea.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="66">66 And all they that had heard <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> laid <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> up in their hearts, saying, What manner of child shall this be? And the hand of the Lord was with him.<ns0:note place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>fear</ns0:hi> here is to be understood, an awe, and Religious reve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rence of God caused by these miraculous operations, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 2.43. <ns0:hi>Fear came upon every soul, and many Wonders, and Signs were done by the Apostles, [these sayings]</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. It is an <ns0:hi>Hebraism,</ns0:hi> these doings, or matters, or things were published throughout all the Parts of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> adjacent to the City, where <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> dwelt <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 39. And those serious People that heard them, pondered on them, considering the work of the Lord, and did think. That this <ns0:hi>Child</ns0:hi> would prove no ordinary Person. <ns0:hi>And the hand of the Lord was with him.</ns0:hi> By the hand of the Lord is meant, the <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> of the Lord, his Providence, <ns0:hi>Love, favour,</ns0:hi> thus the Lord is said to have been with <ns0:hi>Samuel,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 3.19. The hand of the Lord oft signifieth the Power, help, and assistance of the Lord 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 28.19. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 80.17. <ns0:hi>The hand of the Lord</ns0:hi> upon a Person, sometimes signifieth the <ns0:hi>Spirit of Prophecy Ezek</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 1.3. <ns0:hi>&.</ns0:hi> 40.1. but this is a different Phrase, denoting only Gods special favour to <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> watching over and protecting him, using him to grow up and thrive to improve in knowledge, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="67">67 And his father Zacharias was filled with the holy Ghost, and prophesied, saying,<ns0:note place="bottom">We must not think that <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> was before this time desti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tute of the Holy Ghost, we heard the contrary before <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6. but the Holy Ghost at this time came upon him, by a particular, and more especial impulse<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> as it did upon the <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> whom the Spirit moved but at some special times to <ns0:hi>Prophecy,</ns0:hi> tho it at all times dwelt, and wrought in them, as an holy sanctifying Spirit, this is made good by the next Words, which tell us he <ns0:hi>Prophecied,</ns0:hi> which Word signifieth any speaking for, or instead of another, and is not only applicable to such speakings, as are foretel<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ngs of things which shall afterward come to pass, but unto any speaking, for<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or instead of God, in the <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> of his will made known unto us<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> In this <ns0:hi>Prophecy</ns0:hi> there is both predictions o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> what should come to p<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ss concerning <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>concerning Christ,</ns0:hi> and also applications of what was before spoken of them, by the Prop<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ets, and it is observed by some, that it is an <ns0:hi>Epitome</ns0:hi> of all those ancient <ns0:hi>Prophecies,</ns0:hi> and that there is in it, a <ns0:hi>compen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dium</ns0:hi> of the whole Doctrine of the Gospel.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="68">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:295" />68 Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he hath <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.16.</ns0:note> visited and redeemed his people.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="69">69 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 132.17.</ns0:note> And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="70">70 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 23.6.</ns0:note> As he spake by the mouth of his holy pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, which have been since the world began.<ns0:note place="bottom">God is not the God of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> only, but of all the Nations of the Earth also, but he is peculiarly called the God of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> both here and in many other places, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 41.13 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 72.18 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 106.48<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> in regard of the <ns0:hi>Covenant</ns0:hi> which he had specially made with them, and the special advantages they had mentioned by the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 3.2. <ns0:hi>To them were commited the Oracles of God,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.4. to them pertained <ns0:hi>the Adoption, the Glory, the Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nants,</ns0:hi> the giving <ns0:hi>of the Law, and the service of God, and the promises. Zacharias</ns0:hi> pronounceth God <ns0:hi>Blessed,</ns0:hi> and desires that he may be <ns0:hi>Blessed,</ns0:hi> that is honoured, and celebrated, and spoken well of for that he had visited and <ns0:hi>redeemed</ns0:hi> his People. The Word may be extended to all Gods deliverances of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> but it seemeth to be here more specially restrained, by what followeth to the <ns0:hi>Redemption by Christ. And hath raised up an horn of Sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation for them.</ns0:hi> An horn of Salvation, signifies a <ns0:hi>mighty power<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />f<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ll Salvation,</ns0:hi> by a Metaphor taken from Beasts, which much exert their Power by their Horns. The Beasts <ns0:hi>ten horns. Dan.</ns0:hi> 7.7. are expounded to be ten Kings <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24. so where <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> saith he will cut of all the <ns0:hi>Horns of the Wicked,</ns0:hi> so <ns0:hi>Lam.</ns0:hi> 2.3. where God is said to have cut off <ns0:hi>all the Horn of Israel, in the house of his servant David,</ns0:hi> this agreeth to the Prophecy <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 30.9. where Christ is called <ns0:hi>David, They shall serve the Lord their God, and</ns0:hi> David <ns0:hi>their King, whom I will raise unto them,</ns0:hi> who is also called <ns0:hi>a righteous bra<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>h</ns0:hi> raised unto <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi> God is said to have <ns0:hi>raised up this Horn of Salvation</ns0:hi> in the house of <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi> The House of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was now down lapsed, and decayed. God promiseth to raise up to the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> a mighty salvation from the house of <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi> This was fulfilled in Christ, <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s he spake by the mouth of his holy Prophets, which have been since the World began.</ns0:hi> All the Prophets, or many of them at least Prophecied of Christ, as the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> and of a great Salvation to be raised up to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> from his house.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="71">71 That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="72">72 To perform the mercy <ns0:hi>promised</ns0:hi> to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant.<ns0:note place="bottom">This was that which God had told them by his Prophets, that a mighty Salvation, should arise to them out of the house of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> by which they should be saved from their Enemies. By which Enemies the generality of the Jews understood their tempo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Enemies, made of Flesh, and Blood. But <ns0:hi>Zachariah</ns0:hi> speak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing by the Spirit of Prophecy, must needs have a truer Notion of it, as it signifies our spiritual Enemies. All this is attributed to <ns0:hi>Gods Mercy,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>faithfulness,</ns0:hi> his Mercy freely looking upon his Creatures in Distress, and Misery, his <ns0:hi>faithfulness</ns0:hi> in remembrance of his holy Covenant, made to <ns0:hi>Adam, Abraham, David,</ns0:hi> &c. but it is more particularly explained.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="73">73 The oath which he sware to our father <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 12.3.</ns0:note> A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />braham.<ns0:note place="margin">Heb. 6.13.17.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">God first gave <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> his Word, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 18.18. then he confirm<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed it by his Oath. <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 22.16. the Apostle to the <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>When God made promise to</ns0:hi> Abraham, <ns0:hi>because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="74">74 That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 9.14.</ns0:note> might serve him without fear,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="75">75 In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.<ns0:note place="bottom">Thus <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> by an infallible Spirit, expounds the <ns0:hi>Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nants,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Oaths</ns0:hi> of God to <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> not as they appear to us at first view, as if they were promises of a meer tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />poral Kingdom, and a Victory for the Jews over their Enemies, together with a splendid state for them; which was all the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> and the generality of the Jews expected from the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> but as confirming Gods resolution to send the Jews a Saviour, who should save them from their Sins, the guilt and Dominion of them, and from the Power of Hell, and purchase a spiritual liberty for them to serve the Lord all their days, without fear in holiness, and righteousness, which indeed, was the true end of the <ns0:hi>Messiahs</ns0:hi> coming. Thus far now the Song of this holy Man respected Christ, whom he sheweth to be sent from the free Grace, and Mercy of God, yet in performance of Gods truth and faithfulness, according to his Oath, and promises, and to be there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore sent to deliver his People from their Enemies, and to purchase for them a spiritual liberty not to Sin, but to serve the Lord without fear, in Holiness and Righteousness. The latter part of his Prophecy, respecteth <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> the new born Son of this Priest, and heavenly Prophet.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="76">76 And thou child shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mal. 3.1.4.5. <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 17.</ns0:note> thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> here foretelleth what came to pass, about thirty years after (for it cannot be thought that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> began his Ministry, before the Sacerdotal age, especially considering Christ did not begin sooner <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.23. <ns0:hi>Thou shalt be called a Prophet</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that may either signify, <ns0:hi>thou shalt be a Prophet,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 5.9. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.12. or thou shalt be owned, or taken notice of<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> as <ns0:hi>the Prophet of the Highest.</ns0:hi> Both were true in <ns0:hi>Iohn.</ns0:hi> He was a <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> (tho not that Prophet, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.21.) yea and <ns0:hi>more then a Prophet,</ns0:hi> saith our Saviour <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.9, <ns0:hi>And thou shalt go before his face to pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pare his ways.</ns0:hi> This was according to the Prophecy, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40.3. <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 4.5. and according to what <ns0:hi>Ioh<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> said of himself, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.3. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 1.3. See the Notes on <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 3.3.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="77">77 To give knowledge of salvation unto his people, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.3.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>f<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>r.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> by the remission of their sins.<ns0:note place="bottom">To Preach the Doctrine of repentance to Men, that they may ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain remision of Sins. But it seems more natural. To teach People that the only way by which they can attain Salvation, is not by any righteousness of their own, but by obtaining the free Pardon, and remission of their Sins, by Christ and his Righteosness: <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 32.1. which is in short to Preach the Gospel, which <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.16. <ns0:hi>is the Power of God to Salvation to every one that believeth. For therein is the Righteousness of God revealed, from Faith to Faith.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="78">78 Through the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the bowels of Mercy.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> tender mercy of our god; whereby <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the East.</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>Sun rising.</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>Branch.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 24.17. Isa. 11.1. Zech. 6.12.</ns0:note> the day-spring from on high hath visited us.<ns0:note place="bottom">In the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> it is, <ns0:hi>through the bowels of Mercy.</ns0:hi> An ordinary expression, and very natural to signify great, and deep compassion, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 43.30. 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 3.26. Our remission of Sin floweth from Gods bowels of Mercy, it dependeth not upon our satisfactions and penances, (as <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> dream,) but Gods free and tender love, yet God must be just, and declare his righteousness, while <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e justifieth the ungodly therefore. The Day Spring from an high hath visited us <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Some think that the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> Word answereth the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> Word, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 23.5. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 3.8. translated the <ns0:hi>Branch,</ns0:hi> the seventy Interpreters translate it by <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 33.15. Those Texts manifestly relate to Christ, who is called there <ns0:hi>the Branch.</ns0:hi> Others think it rather answereth the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> Word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> we translate it a great <ns0:hi>Light.</ns0:hi> Others think, it should be translated the <ns0:hi>East.</ns0:hi> So they say Christ is called <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 3.9.6.12. but we translate it the <ns0:hi>Branch</ns0:hi> in both those places. Be it the <ns0:hi>Branch,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Light,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Day Spring,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>East,</ns0:hi> it is certain Christ is meant, who is called the <ns0:hi>Son of Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness, Mal.</ns0:hi> 4.2. That God might be just in the remission of our Sins, he sent Christ to visit us, and in our Nature to dye for us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="79">79 To give light to them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.<ns0:note place="bottom">Here <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> sheweth us the end, why God visited us, with his Son, the <ns0:hi>Branch,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Light,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Day Spring, the Son of Righteousness,</ns0:hi> Men were in the darkness of Sin, and ignorance, dead in trespasses and Sins, at War and enmity with God, Christ came to give them the <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> of Gospel <ns0:hi>Revelations,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Spiritual comfort,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Salvation,</ns0:hi> to purchase <ns0:hi>Peace,</ns0:hi> and to direct them how to walk that they might have Peace with God, and at last <ns0:hi>enter into Peace.</ns0:hi> This he did to the Jews first, then to the Gentiles, see <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 9.1, 2 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 60.1.19.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="80">80 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 2.4<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 3.1.</ns0:note> was in the deserts till the day of his shewing unto Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Evangelists having done with <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> his Prophetical Song, now cometh to tell us, what became of <ns0:hi>Iohn.</ns0:hi> He saith, the <ns0:hi>Child grew,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>waxed strong in Spirit.</ns0:hi> He did not only grow in his bodily dimensions, but in the endowments of his Mind<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>and was in the deserts,</ns0:hi> that is in places very thinly inha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bited, (some will have this to have been the deserts of <ns0:hi>Ziph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Maon) till the day of his shewing to</ns0:hi> Israel. That is (in all probability) till he was about <ns0:hi>thirty years of age,</ns0:hi> when he came forth, as a Publick Preacher to those parts of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> where he spent the small remaining part of his Life, of which we shall hear more hereafter.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
